core_obligations: Set up the truncations (proof lines 5341-5355): write K_n = tau_{>= -n}E and K = R lim K_n, and observe that the claimed isomorphism can be checked on the quotients of the limit filtration, that is on the cohomology sheaves H^{m}(E) restricted to the objects of B.

Apply the vanishing hypothesis (proof lines 5355-5375): the hypothesis says that for objects of B the cohomology of the successive quotients involved vanishes above the bounds p(V, m) over a cofinal system of coverings, so the relevant derived limits of the cohomology vanish by the cofinality criterion of this chapter.

Conclude (proof lines 5375-5389): combining the vanishing with the exact sequences relating the truncations gives that the map E -> K is an isomorphism, since it is an isomorphism on the objects of B and those cover every object.
proof_roadmap: Replace E by the system of its truncations and let K be the derived limit.
Check the map on the successive quotients, which are the cohomology sheaves of E.
Use the vanishing hypothesis over the cofinal system of coverings to kill the relevant derived limits.
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a criterion for an object of D(O) to be recovered as the derived limit of its truncations: it suffices that over a cofinal system of coverings of every object of B the cohomology of the cohomology sheaves vanishes above bounds p(V, m) (statement lines 5319-5339). The proof replaces E by the system K_n = tau_{>= -n}E with K = R lim K_n and checks the map on the successive quotients, which are the cohomology sheaves (proof lines 5341-5355); the hypothesis then kills the relevant derived limits through the cofinality criterion of this chapter (proof lines 5355-5375), and the covering condition on B upgrades the pointwise vanishing to the isomorphism (proof lines 5375-5389). The non-formal content is the bookkeeping of the truncations against the bounds p(V, m). The claim is H2: one reduction to cohomology sheaves plus one application of the vanishing criterion.
